column9: Generally, an LLM can infer my intent from the code changes I make. However, it sometimes misses implicit motivations—for example, when a refactor is executed to prepare for a future requirement. In those cases I need to provide additional background. For public GitHub projects, LLM tools can usually retrieve and interpret that context via the `gh` CLI; for internal corporate projects, by contrast, obtaining and consolidating the necessary context is more complex and requires extra engineering effort to make the end-to-end workflow reliable.
column10: In practice, current LLM-generated commit messages are often too granular, so I frequently have to manually trim and refine them. Having controls — for example, sliders to tune verbosity, tone, or focus — would make generation much more usable. Alternatively, producing multiple candidate messages at once so I can pick the best one would also be helpful.
